newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras says in no hurry to extradite Haitian to US.
newsitem.headline: Honduras says in no hurry to extradite Haitian to US.

text.p: The high court of Honduras said on Wednesday it was in no hurry to extradite former Haitian police colonel Joseph Michel Francois, wanted by Washington on drug-trafficking charges.

Washington has been trying since April to have Haiti's former head of police stand trial in a U.S. court, and his defence laywers say Washington has been pressuring Honduras to speed up the extradition process.
"No one is pushing us, we have no deadline, and the judicial authorities have to take their time (to resolve this)," Miguel Rivera, president of the supreme court of justice, told reporters.
The Honduran court turned down a U.S. extradition request on April 16, saying Washington had insufficient evidence against the Haitian.
The U.S. embassy in the Honduran capital has appealed against the decision, but so far without result. Court officials, however, said a decision could be taken next week.
Court officials said the Haitian's defence had been misinformed or was acting in bad faith when it said Washington was exerting pressure to have Francois judged in the United States.
Francois was the much feared chief of police in the Haitian capital Port-au-Prince during the 1991-94 military government.
He arrived in Honduras in April 1996 and was arrested by Honduran police backed by U.S. agents.

U.S. drug enforcement officials had planned to bring him straight to Miami and into court and were dismayed when Honduran legal authorities held up the operation as he was being escorted to the airport.

Washington says Francois used his position as police chief to turn Haiti into a vast staging-post to ship thouands of pounds of cocaine and heroin into the United States, in league with Colombian drug barons.

He is also believed to be the mastermind behind the 1991 coup that toppled Jean Bertrand Aristide. As police chief he created a network of plain-clothed policemen who terrorised opponents of the regime.
